\chapter{Learning Theory — Bernstein}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.LearningTheory.JohnsonLindenstrauss.Bernstein
\section{Overview}

This module develops a two-parameter sub-exponential MGF condition,
\texttt{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF}, and derives from it
one-sided, other-sided, and two-sided Bernstein-type concentration
inequalities.  The main application is a tail bound for the deviation
of $\sum_i Y_i^2$ from its mean $n\sigma^2$ for an independent
identically-distributed family, which serves as the central reusable
tool for Johnson--Lindenstrauss-style concentration arguments.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Bernstein MGF condition]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF}
\label{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF}
\leanok
$\texttt{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF}\ X\ \mu\ c\ t_{\max}$ is a
predicate on a random variable $X : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$, a measure
$\mu$, and real parameters $c, t_{\max} \ge 0$.  It asserts that for
every $t$ with $|t| \le t_{\max}$, the exponential moment
$e^{tX}$ is $\mu$-integrable, and the moment generating function
satisfies $\mathbf{E}_\mu[e^{tX}] \le e^{c t^2}$.  The pair
$(c, t_{\max})$ parametrizes a ``two-parameter sub-exponential'' family:
$c$ controls the quadratic growth near zero and $t_{\max}$ bounds the
radius of validity.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Sub-exponential MGF bound for independent sums]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF.sum_of_iIndepFun}
\label{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF.sum_of_iIndepFun}
\leanok
\uses{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF}
\difficulty{4}
Let $(X_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be a family of measurable real random variables on a
probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$ that are mutually independent, and let $s$ be a finite
set of indices. Fix a radius $t_{\max}$, and suppose that for each $i \in s$ there is a
constant $c_i$ such that $e^{tX_i}$ is $\mu$-integrable and $\mathbf{E}_\mu[e^{tX_i}]
\le e^{c_i t^2}$ for every $t$ with $|t| \le t_{\max}$. Then the sum $\sum_{i \in s}
X_i$ satisfies the same two-parameter sub-exponential bound with radius $t_{\max}$ and
constant $\sum_{i \in s} c_i$: for every $t$ with $|t| \le t_{\max}$, the moment $e^{t
\sum_{i \in s} X_i}$ is $\mu$-integrable and $\mathbf{E}_\mu\!\left[e^{t \sum_{i \in s}
X_i}\right] \le e^{(\sum_{i \in s} c_i)\, t^2}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Upper-tail Bernstein bound]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF.measure_ge_le}
\label{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF.measure_ge_le}
\leanok
\uses{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF}
\difficulty{4}
Let $X : \Omega \to \bbr$ be a random variable on a finite measure space $(\Omega,
\mu)$, and suppose $X$ satisfies the Bernstein moment-generating-function condition with
parameters $c$ and $t_{\max}$: for every $t$ with $\abs{t} \le t_{\max}$ the exponential
moment $e^{tX}$ is $\mu$-integrable and $\E_\mu[e^{tX}] \le e^{c t^2}$. If $c > 0$, then
for every $s$ with $0 \le s \le 2c\,t_{\max}$ the upper tail obeys
\[
  \mu\bigl(\{\omega : s \le X(\omega)\}\bigr) \;\le\; \exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{s^2}{4c}\Bigr).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Lower-tail Bernstein bound]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF.measure_le_le}
\label{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF.measure_le_le}
\leanok
\uses{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF}
\difficulty{4}
Let $X : \Omega \to \bbr$ be a random variable on a probability space carrying a finite
measure $\mu$, and suppose $X$ satisfies the Bernstein moment generating function
condition with parameters $c$ and $t_{\max}$: for every $t$ with $|t| \le t_{\max}$, the
exponential moment $e^{tX}$ is $\mu$-integrable and $\E_\mu[e^{tX}] \le e^{c t^2}$. If
$c > 0$, then for every $s$ with $0 \le s \le 2 c\, t_{\max}$,
\[
\mu\bigl(\{\omega \mid X(\omega) \le -s\}\bigr) \;\le\;
\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{s^2}{4c}\Bigr).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Two-sided Bernstein tail bound]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF.measure_abs_gt_le}
\label{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF.measure_abs_gt_le}
\leanok
\uses{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF, ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF.measure_ge_le, ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF.measure_le_le}
\difficulty{4}
Let $X : \Omega \to \bbr$ be a random variable on a probability space $(\Omega, \mu)$,
and let $c, t_{\max} \ge 0$ be real parameters such that $X$ satisfies the Bernstein
moment generating function condition with parameters $c$ and $t_{\max}$: for every $t$
with $\abs{t} \le t_{\max}$ the exponential moment $e^{tX}$ is $\mu$-integrable and
$\E_\mu[e^{tX}] \le e^{c t^2}$. If $c > 0$, then for every $s$ with $0 \le s \le 2 c\,
t_{\max}$,
\[
\mu\bigl(\{\omega \mid s < \abs{X(\omega)}\}\bigr) \;\le\;
2\exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{s^2}{4c}\Bigr).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bernstein tail bound for a sum of centered squares]
\lean{ProbabilityTheory.centered_squared_iid_tail}
\label{ProbabilityTheory.centered_squared_iid_tail}
\leanok
\uses{ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF, ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF.measure_abs_gt_le, ProbabilityTheory.HasBernsteinMGF.sum_of_iIndepFun}
\difficulty{5}
Let $(Y_i)_{i}$ be a finite family of measurable real random variables on a probability
space $(\Omega, \mu)$, indexed by a finite set of cardinality $n$, and suppose the $Y_i$
are mutually independent. Fix real numbers $\sigma^2$, $c > 0$, and $t_{\max}$, and
suppose that for each $i$ the centered square $Y_i^2 - \sigma^2$ satisfies the Bernstein
MGF condition with parameters $c$ and $t_{\max}$. Then for every $s$ with $0 \le s \le 2
n c\, t_{\max}$,
\[
  \mu\!\left(\left\{\omega \;\middle|\;
    s < \left|\sum_{i} Y_i(\omega)^2 - n\sigma^2\right|\right\}\right)
  \;\le\;
  2\exp\!\left(-\frac{s^2}{4 n c}\right).
\]
\end{lemma}
